title: Crediting Promotional Interest Left Unpaid by a Closed Statement Cycle
content:
### When this applies

Where promotional interest stands owed on an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts for a statement cycle that has already closed, that promotional interest is settled on the account as a correction to that cycle.

### What is booked

A single promotional interest entry is credited to the account, marked as a bank error correction and carrying the statement cycle it belongs to. The account's posted balance rises by the amount credited on the spot, and the customer sees a new promotional interest line with today's posting date, the corrected cycle shown against it, and a balance higher by that amount.

### Recording the correction

The correction is recorded with the tool `post_promotional_interest_correction_acb0ec5b`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call posts one promotional interest entry.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `savings_account_id` | the reference number of the savings or money market account the promotional interest is credited to, taken from the savings account lookup | an account reference number |
| `customer_id` | the customer reference number of the account owner, taken from the customer profile lookup | a customer reference number |
| `statement_cycle` | the statement cycle the unpaid promotional interest belongs to, being the month in which that cycle closed | written as YYYY-MM; an empty value is not accepted |
| `correction_amount` | the promotional interest being credited | USD to 2 decimal places, always positive; a value carrying more than 2 decimal places is stored rounded half up to the cent, and the bank's own Eastern Time posting date is used |

### What the call returns

A confirmation sentence carrying the reference number of the promotional interest entry just created, the credited amount in USD to two decimal places, the statement cycle it was booked against, and the account's new posted balance in USD to two decimal places. Receiving that sentence is what indicates the credit completed.
